E1.evidence: PR #157 (Jmeyer1292) reports a reproduction with ur_driver's test_move.py test_interrupt routine: "when interrupted with a new trajectory while still executing a previous trajectory, the robot would immediately jump to the first point of the new trajectory." Maintainer abubeck: "I have tested this. Therefore I will merge it."

E2.evidence: The defect is a wrong argument to driver.py's own helper: in URTrajectoryFollower.on_goal() the parent revision calls point0 = sample_traj(self.traj, now) with now = time.time(), while sample_traj(traj, t) expects an offset into the trajectory (every other call passes now - self.traj_t0). The wrong sample is computed and consumed inside the driver node when it splices the new goal; the action client's goal and the robot-side program behave correctly and any correct peer would receive the same wrong setpoint. Fix bcac4f5: point0 = sample_traj(self.traj, now - self.traj_t0). PR text: "It used the absolute time (from time.time()) instead of the offset into the previous trajectory which is used in every other call of this particular function."

E3.evidence: Not evaluated as a composition: E2 stopped at step 2 (internal).

E4.evidence: PR #157: "running the test_interrupt routine caused a UR10 arm to emergency stop fairly consistently" and "the robot would immediately jump to the first point of the new trajectory."

notes: Reporter environment: "I did my testing on a UR5 running firmware version 3.0.x and the Hydro-devel branch of universal robot." Fix commit bcac4f5 (2015-01-29) merged into hydro-devel as b3c2c21 (2015-03-12).
